matches.quote: Notation is inconsistent. Figs. S4–S5 use T_FPS and T_OCO against T_C and T_COO in the main text, and T_IM and T_MI are used interchangeably; unify the labels.
JT intensity is assumed, not shown, to measure the AFMI-COO phase fraction, and Fig. 5 has no quantitative input... estimate COO/FMM fractions
A warming excursion into T_C < T_T < T_COO converting FMM to COO, which then stays arrested on fast recooling, appears to account for the observations.
Methods says "cyclic procedure, depicted in figure 1 a"; it should be Fig. 1b.
Before attributing the threefold change in ρ (Fig. 4d) to bulk phase reconfiguration, the authors should provide four-probe resistivity for at least one cycle
The laser-heating temperature scale is calibrated with the observable under study, with no independent thermometer, and its uncertainty is understated.
repeat the Fig. 3 protocol with the cold-finger heater cycling between 38 K and the same T_T values at fixed low laser power (10 mW)
"Non-volatile" is also untested: there is no retention measurement of ρ, M or Raman intensity at T_B over time
State in the main text that the Bose–Einstein factor was not removed (Fig. S1 caption), since Fig. 2d compares intensities across temperatures.
close to the "spurious peak" (~660–670 cm⁻¹) marked in red in Fig. 2a... which the authors attribute "possibly" to oxygen vacancies without evidence
The authors should also report the cooling rate or time constant after a power step.
the neuromorphic/quantum-device framing in the abstract and conclusions should be justified or toned down to match a single-sample, bulk, cryogenic study.
No laser-free control shows that the Raman memory is thermal... Either the laser-heated spot is not equivalent to a uniformly heated sample, or the laser does more than heat.

notes: C16 and P10 identify the same erroneous reference to 'figure 1 a' in the Methods paragraph on magnetic and electric properties (the referee reading it as referring to the M and R data in Fig. 4, the review as referring to the cycling protocol in Fig. 1b). For C2, the review explicitly asks for the cooling rate/time constant after a laser power step (P4) and discusses spatial thermal gradients (P15) and base-power dwell conditions (P16), but does not ask for the ramp-up or target dwell times, so it is scored as 'partly'.
